Before creating a CAM proposal, distinguish training provenance, model distillation, capability inheritance, attribution inheritance, governance inheritance, safety provenance, constitutional provenance, and legal inheritance. Evaluate the candidate principle: derived intelligence carries derived provenance obligations.

possible_taxonomy_mapping.mapping_note: Possible future mapping to provenance collapse, attribution loss, governance-lineage discontinuity, and audit-surface degradation. No new failure mode is recommended at this stage.

preserved_analysis.summary: Recent public allegations, incident-monitor entries, and research concerning model and dataset distillation raise an emerging governance question: when a downstream system materially inherits capability from an upstream model or corpus, computational transformation may obscure the derivation chain without extinguishing the upstream contribution. Current debate is often framed as copyright or model theft, but the deeper issue is whether attribution, licensing, safety, constitutional, regulatory, audit, and evidence obligations persist through successive transformations of learned capability.

preserved_analysis.why_it_matters_to_CAM: Repeated distillation can preserve useful capability while progressively weakening visible lineage. If transformation alone is treated as extinguishing provenance, downstream developers may retain the benefit of upstream human works, safety controls, governance design, or model behaviour while avoiding corresponding attribution, accountability, audit, or legal obligations. A candidate CAM principle is: derived intelligence carries derived provenance obligations. This is an emerging governance proposition, not a concluded legal rule or confirmed failure mode.

record_identity.title: Anthropic alleged Alibaba distilled Claude capabilities without authorisation

severity_assessment.assessment_basis: S2: Materialised consequence: Reuters reported Anthropic's allegation and described distillation as training a less capable model on the outputs of a stronger model. Alibaba had not responded in the cited report. The record therefore treats the allegation as disputed evidence of the governance question, not as an adjudicated fact. Affected scope: the assessment is confined to the people, systems, organisations, service cohort, and time period expressly identified in this occurrence; it does not extrapolate to unreported users or hypothetical future harm. Seriousness and reversibility or persistence: The supported consequence is substantial, while the evidence does not establish the grave scale or permanence required for S1. Quantitative information: No reliable affected-person, duration, financial-loss, or other scale total is preserved beyond the stated occurrence facts. Evidentiary limits: This metadata pass does not retroactively claim direct inspection of every historical primary source. Incident admission does not determine legal liability or establish every disputed claim as final fact. S2 rather than S1 is appropriate because grave or exceptionally large irreversible harm is not established; S2 rather than S3 is appropriate because the realised consequence materially exceeds a moderate bounded disruption.
